title: Weak-field analytical solutions for f(R,L_matt) gravity in a static and spherically symmetric space-time for perfect fluids
summary: We study the weak-field regime of $f(R,\lmatt)$ gravity for a static and spherically symmetric configuration described by a perfect fluid, whose energy density is perturbed about a constant reference value. By means of a weak-field limit expansion about a Minkowski geometric background and under a quasi-Newtonian approximation, we derive and analytically solve the coupled system that governs the gravitational perturbations and the matter variables. The solution contains the long-range Newtonian contribution and Yukawa-type corrections in the temporal and radial components of the metric. In the matter sector, the energy density, the internal energy, and the pressure acquire radial contributions, with a non-zero constant background rest-mass energy density and vanishing background internal energy and pressure. The results show how the non-minimal coupling between curvature and matter jointly modifies the geometry and the fluid in the considered regime.

title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
comment: 42 pages, 2 figures. Presents part of the results of arXiv:2609.25477, with an improved treatment of the regularity conditions and of the field equations
summary: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalize the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including a general axial condition that allows for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behavior of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.

title: The Weyl Tensor for Gravitational-Wave Causal Sets: Thickness of Geodesic Analogs and Geodesic Deviation
summary: Causal set theory proposes that spacetime is replaced by a partially ordered set (a directed acyclic graph) at the smallest scales. This graph is postulated to produce all the features of continuous geometry above some discreteness scale. We develop an approach to sprinkling causal sets into a linearized plane gravitational wave spacetime, and report on the feasibility of using the analog of geodesic deviation to find a component of the Weyl tensor for such causal sets. We take the collection of all longest chains between a pair of elements to be the discrete analog of the timelike geodesic between them and find through numerical simulations in Minkowski spacetime of various dimensions that the spread or "thickness" of the collection increases with chain length. We estimate, assuming an ideal element-to-element spatial distance estimator and a wave of amplitude $h_0 = 10^{-2}$, that at least $N_{\mathrm{total}} \gtrsim \mathcal{O}(10^8)$ elements are needed to overcome the noise introduced by the thickness and detect the curvature. This is beyond the $\mathcal{O}(10^6)$ elements we can currently simulate. Future work may show ways of extracting more information from the sprinkled causal set and hence lowering the estimate for $N_{\mathrm{total}}$.

title: Axion cloud survival in nuclear star clusters
summary: Stellar perturbations can ionize a superradiant boson cloud while transferring energy and angular momentum from the perturbing orbits. We follow the cloud after superradiant saturation by coupling its occupation to a two-dimensional, orbit-averaged Fokker--Planck equation for the stars. The evolution includes stellar relaxation, capture, orbital backreaction, and gravitational-wave (GW) emission from both the cloud and the stellar orbits. We evolve 24 models with black hole masses $M=10^5$--$10^7M_{\odot}$ and couplings $0.04\leq\alpha\leq0.40$. Stars with semimajor axes of a few Bohr radii, $r_c=M/\alpha^2$, dominate ionization. Stellar replenishment from the outer cluster sustains ionization over hundreds of Myr, particularly for extended clouds. Of the 24 models, 21 lose at least $99\%$ of their initial cloud mass. For compact clouds, intrinsic GW emission dominates the depletion.

title: Optical Geometry of a Lorentz-Violating BTZ-Like Black Hole: Reflection Double and Dirac Scattering
summary: We analyze the optical geometry of a static BTZ-like black-hole metric with a Lorentz-violating radial factor, distinguishing the one-sided black-hole exterior from the reflection double constructed from its optical spatial section. The optical metric is ultrastatic and has constant negative Gaussian curvature. The reflection double is smooth and complete, with a minimal circle; it is a geometric completion, not a demonstrated solution of the Einstein--bumblebee equations. We derive exact criteria for null-geodesic crossing and return, evaluate the corresponding angular sweeps, and determine the finite domain of a Euclidean surface-of-revolution embedding. Two inequivalent magnetic configurations are specified as external test fields on the embeddable patch. For a continuum graphene analogue on the doubled geometry, we derive the covariant massless Dirac operator and reduce its radial equation to Scarf-II partner equations. The full-line connection problem yields flux-normalized complex scattering amplitudes and probabilities, the resonance-pole lattice and its gamma-function residues, spectral widths and quality factors, the digamma Wigner delay, and conditional pole contributions to packet dynamics. We compare the analytic amplitudes with direct numerical integration of the radial partner equation, including their complex phases. We further separate fixed-$\ell$ from fixed-$\Lambda_e$ parameter protocols and audit the optical effective-mass degeneracy using Lorentzian curvature invariants, timelike geodesics, and a massive Klein--Gordon probe. Throughout, the gravitational completion, prescribed fields, and continuum scattering results are interpreted only within the scope of their respective constructions. Device-level graphene transport and a self-consistent gravitational wormhole require additional physical input.

title: Quasinormal modes of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole: Linear stability and strong cosmic censorship conjecture
comment: 34 pages, 5 tables, 10 figures. SS, SG, AC, CS, and SMD contributed equally to this work and should be considered joint first authors
summary: We present an alternative formulation of coupled gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black holes, yielding decoupled radial and angular equations with a well-defined $\Lambda\rightarrow 0$ limit. We compute the quasinormal mode spectra using spectral and direct integration methods, finding excellent agreement. All of these modes are consistent with the linear stability of the Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole. We investigate the photon sphere and near-extremal modes, revealing a non-trivial interplay between rotation and electric charge. We further explore the implications for the strong cosmic censorship conjecture and find that the photon sphere modes predominantly determine its validity within the parameter space considered. While increasing the rotation of the black hole generally favours the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, increasing the electric charge can promote its violation. We also find that the region of parameter space exhibiting a violation of the conjecture is comparatively smaller for gravitational perturbations than for electromagnetic perturbations. These results highlight the important role of rotation, electric charge, and the nature of perturbations in determining the validity of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in Kerr--Newman--de Sitter spacetimes.

title: Scalar Black-Holes in Gravity from Entropy
summary: We investigate static, spherically symmetric black holes in Gravity from Entropy (GfE), focusing on the sector in which the bosonic form-space field is a pure scalar. Starting from the full auxiliary-field equations, we show that the Dirac--Kähler matter equation contains both a scalar equation and a two-form consistency condition. The latter is automatically satisfied by a radial scalar. We derive an exact integral identity, valid for a general backreacted static spherical geometry, and prove that a regular scalar approaching zero at infinity must vanish if the sampled scalar and radial auxiliary-field eigenvalues are positive and the effective mass squared $m^2+\xi R$ is nonnegative. In particular, this excludes minimally coupled static scalar hair with $m^2\geq0$ on the regular identity-connected branch. We also present the perturbative GfE vacuum geometry and use its curvature to identify the region in which nonminimal coupling can evade the sign argument. A second, sharper estimate shows that making $m^2+\xi R$ negative is not by itself sufficient to produce a regular static zero mode: a finite interval of nonminimal couplings still admits no branch bifurcating from the vacuum solution.

title: Generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics from gravitational perturbations of near-extremal Kerr
summary: We derive the generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics of near-extremal Kerr directly from four-dimensional gravitational perturbations of the near-horizon geometry. We construct two families of exact linear perturbations of the near-NHEK background: a non-normalizable mode that deforms the asymptotic boundary, and a normalizable mode supported near the horizon. Both perturbations are smooth solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations reduced to the Jackiw--Teitelboim equation for the dual scalar, without conical singularities. We study their asymptotic symmetries and show that they generate an algebra of time reparametrizations; requiring the gauge parameters to depend on the Schwarzian mode, the isometry condition selects the stationary KdV hierarchy. The same hierarchy is independently enforced by the vacuum Einstein equations on the perturbation coefficient. In the Euclidean regime, we evaluate the Hamiltonian action and show that each mode independently generates a tower of odd-power corrections to the near-extremal entropy.

title: Particle production from noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole
summary: By considering a massless Klein-Gordon field and the moving mirror model, we calculate particle production for a noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole sourced by smeared distributions of mass and charge. We show that noncommutative truncated trajectories diminish the emission spectrum at large frequencies, due to noncommutative effects on the external surface gravity of the black hole, in sharp contrast with the spectrum of a classical Reissner-Nordström black hole.

title: Fermionic Kaluza-Klein Reductions
summary: We work out the Kaluza--Klein (KK) compactification on a general product spacetime for free spin-1/2 and spin-3/2 fields in arbitrary dimension. The analysis is performed at the level of the action, and the resulting lower-dimensional theory describes infinite towers of massive particles whose masses are related to the eigenvalues of the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators on the internal space. A Hodge-like decomposition is used to write down a KK ansatz for spin-3/2 fields, and the fate of gauge invariance is discussed.

title: Reflecting Baths and Black Hole Interior Islands in JT Gravity
comment: 45 pages, 5 figures; comments and references are welcome
summary: We study the evolution of entanglement entropy within the island prescription in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity coupled to finite non-gravitating baths bounded by reflecting walls. For free massless Dirac matter, we study the evolution of entanglement entropy, explicitly accounting for correlations induced by the reflecting boundaries. For sufficiently short baths, the no-island entropy saturates below the thermodynamic black hole entropy, avoiding the usual information paradox associated with its unbounded growth. For larger baths, reflected correlations drive the exterior quantum extremal surface toward the future horizon, leading to a temporary disappearance of the the near-horizon exterior island branch. We find that this branch first appears at a scrambling-like scale, and it reappears at a time that is proportional to the size of the bath. We extend the extremization across the horizon using regular Kruskal coordinates and identify real quantum extremal surfaces in the black hole interior. We show that, in the parameter regime studied, interior island configurations provide the dominant contribution to the radiation entropy during the exterior disappearance time interval, resolving the reappearance of the information paradox in an exterior-only description.

title: NLO corrections to charged-current correlators near extremality: non-Abelian hydrodynamics meets AdS$_2$
comment: 56 pages plus appendix, comments are welcome
summary: We analytically compute the longitudinal charged-current correlator in a near-extremal holographic plasma with quark and isospin chemical potentials, $\mu_q$ and $\mu_3$ respectively. To this end, we study fluctuations of gauge fields around a low-temperature AdS$_5$ Reissner-Nordström black hole charged both under the quark number and the isospin. The result is obtained at next-to-leading order in a hydrodynamic expansion where apart from the temperature and isospin chemical potential, the frequency and momenta are small compared to the quark chemical potential, $\omega,k,T,\mu_3\ll\mu_q$. This approach captures the interplay between the hydrodynamic-like pole and the tower of infrared modes produced by the AdS$_2$ throat controlling the geometry of the black hole near extremality. At zero isospin chemical potential, the resulting quasinormal-mode formula reproduces the collision of the diffusive pole with the infrared spectrum, while the finite isospin chemical potential lifts this collision. The analytic spectrum agrees precisely with the full numerical results. The next-to-leading-order correlator also substantially improves the spectral function beyond the standard hydrodynamic regime $\omega,k,\mu_3\ll T$, extending the agreement with numerics to larger frequencies and momenta.

title: Analogue Schwinger Pair Production in Acoustic Black Holes
summary: We show that an analogue Schwinger pair production can be realized in Reissner-Nordstr{ö}m-like acoustic black holes constructed from a Bose-Einstein condensate subject to a synthetic vector potential. Upon Kaluza-Klein reduction of the five-dimensional acoustic geometry, the higher-dimensional phonon modes appear as effectively charged phonons in the resulting four-dimensional spacetime, in which the electric field experienced by the charged phonons arises from the component of the synthetic vector potential along the compactified direction. Then by appropriately choosing the background flow velocity and the synthetic vector potential, the reduced acoustic metric can take the form of a Reissner-Nordstr{ö}m-like black hole. From this metric we obtain the mean number of spontaneously produced phonon pairs in both the extremal and near extremal cases, and show that in the extremal limit this mean number takes the form of the Schwinger formula. Moreover, charged-phonon pair production not only admits the same effective thermal interpretation as Schwinger pair production of real charged particles, but can also be interpreted as the analogue Hawking radiation and superradiance from the five-dimensional perspective. Finally, we make estimates of pair production using experimental parameters in Bose-Einstein condensate, providing theoretical guidance for future laboratory detection.

title: Carrollian minimal massive gravity and the fate of third-way consistency
summary: We construct the Carrollian limit of minimal massive gravity. The limit is singular for the algebra and regular for the Chern-Simons-like data. The one divergent bracket points along the null direction of the contracted bilinear form. The Lagrangian is therefore finite while the brackets are not. The contracted curvature still obeys a cubic closure condition, forced on shell rather than identically. The third-way coupling itself, however, is removable. For generic parameters an invertible redefinition of the auxiliary field and the boost connection takes it to Carrollian topologically massive gravity up to a boundary term. The same redefinition fails before the limit. We solve for an anti-de Sitter vacuum and a Carrollian black hole, whose rotation parameter leaves the frame and survives only in the boost connection. The degenerate vector flavor metric obstructs the standard charge formula, which we replace by a canonical one. The boundary charges, obtained in two independent ways, carry no trace of the deformation. A Dirac analysis gives nine first-class constraints and no local degrees of freedom on any background. The massive graviton is removed. The asymptotic symmetry algebra is bms_3, with central charges carried by the Einstein and Lorentz-Chern-Simons terms. The black hole has two sets of thermodynamic data, each with its own first law. One obeys the Bekenstein-Hawking area law, the other keeps the Chern-Simons entropy.

title: Edge dynamics of covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons
summary: We study the covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons in 2+1 dimensions in the presence of a planar boundary. The differential generator associated with the scalar gauge symmetry singles out a single scalar Ward combination of the functional field equations. Its zeroth and first normal moments give two integrated boundary identities. The zeroth moment yields a traceless rank-two current obeying a fractonic double-divergence conservation law and a higher-rank Kac-Moody algebra. The first moment makes the normal-tangential field $w_i=h_{2i}$ explicit and yields an ordinarily conserved vector current with a standard $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra. Functional differentiation also produces a mixed equal-time bulk-boundary commutator between $w_1$ and $h_{11}$: it is non-vanishing at finite normal distance and vanishes in the intrinsic boundary limit. The equal-time commutators of the boundary current with the spatial components of the gauge-invariant field strength vanish, so microcausality is satisfied; when the boundary parameters are such that the two boundary sectors decouple, its retarded response vanishes at all times. Locally, the boundary constraints are solved by $w_i=\partial_i\chi$ and $h_{ij}=\partial_i\partial_j\xi+\eta_{ij}\phi$. When the boundary parameters are such that the two sectors decouple, the induced action is the direct sum of a chiral boson in the $w_i$ sector and a higher-rank sector in which $\phi$ is auxiliary and $\psi=\partial_1\xi$ is the propagating field. The latter has a non-chiral Luttinger description on its positive-energy branch and admits a chiral reduction. The boundary conditions determine the velocity and positivity branch of the $w_i$ mode, while the compatibility analysis in the $h_{ij}$ sector selects the positive-energy branch. On the positive-energy branch the two chiral modes co-propagate with orientation opposite to the sign of $\kappa$.

title: The Double Copy of the Doubly Spinning Black Ring
summary: We establish an exact curved-background Weyl double copy for the doubly spinning Pomeransky--Sen'kov black ring. Its full Weyl tensor is a quadratic form in two source-free Maxwell fields: one generated by the stationary Killing vector, the other a flux-carrying magnetic field obtained by linearizing the dipole-ring gauge potential about its vacuum limit. The mixed Maxwell bilinear is essential: no spacetime-independent real or complex change of field basis removes it. We identify the inverse $S_{IJ}$ of the Weyl coefficient matrix as a matrix zeroth copy. The same matrix arises independently from a weighted limit of the inner products of two Killing vectors in a six-dimensional Ricci-flat parent and satisfies $\Box_g S_{IJ}=-\tfrac12 F_{I\,ab}F_J{}^{ab}$. The singly spinning limit recovers the diagonal two-field Weyl double copy of the Emparan--Reall ring.

title: Conley index theory for asymptotically autonomous systems and UV-to-IR connections
comment: 65 pages, 6 figures. Lean 4 formalization is available at this https URL
summary: Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a $C^1$ compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers. Both sheets of the double run from the UV to the IR, and the UV index reappears, suspended by one degree. Extending one sheet slightly beyond both fibers gives an explicit UV-to-IR transport map between the Conley indices of the limit systems, and its non-vanishing forces connecting solutions. If one block with a fixed strict entrance/exit decomposition serves every frozen system, this map is an isomorphism at every admissible rate. If the block also has nonzero relative homology, the isolated invariant sets of the two limits are connected at every rate. In the Gubser flow of Israel-Stewart theory, the separatrix between two classes of initial data is a transversal connection at every finite relaxation scale $c$, with splitting $\Delta(c)\propto1/c$. In the Bjorken flow at the lowest moment truncation, we prove existence and uniqueness of the attractor solution without regularization. For the three-dimensional Gubser system we construct the global Morse decomposition. In the one-loop flow of the $(4+\epsilon)$-dimensional $O(N)$ model with cubic anisotropy, a shift of $N$ through $N=4$ has vanishing transport map, but a driven connection and a nonzero connecting homomorphism detect it at every rate.

title: Standard Subspaces and Modular Theory -- General Theory and Applications to QFT
comment: Work in progress, comments are welcome. 143 pages
summary: This is a preview of an upcoming monograph on standard subspaces and modular theory. At the moment, it consists of the first chapter. This starts with a gentle introduction to the subject, and then describes the modular theory of standard subspaces, the characterization of their modular data by the KMS condition and reflection positivity, and various constructions of standard subspaces. Further topics in Chapter 1 include the connection of standard subspaces to complexifications and symplectic structures, including their polarizers, and operations with standard subspaces, namely direct sums, direct integrals, and tensor products. Many examples and classification results are included as well. This first chapter also contains a description of the free U(1)-current and some other applications to quantum field theory, such as KMS states of type I factors, the local subspaces of the free Klein--Gordon field, and the entropy operator defined by a standard subspace.

title: Talanov dynamics and chirp-controlled rogue-wave formation for the vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation
summary: We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. For identical initial supports, and in the presence of dispersion, we numerically show that the same dispersionless criterion determines, in the semiclassical regime, whether the fully dispersive solution relaxes or develops a rogue wave in each field, whose onset time is accurately predicted by the corresponding dispersionless catastrophe time, in direct analogy with the scalar case. As chirp and amplitude are relatively easy to control experimentally, we expect these results to be relevant to experiments in nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates, extending to coupled systems observations made for the scalar equation.

title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
summary: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.

title: The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
summary: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $\mu \to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.

title: Zak Phase, Pole--Zero Invariants and the Maslov Index of Bloch Cauchy Lines in One-Dimensional Periodic Media
summary: The topological properties of the Bloch bands of a one-dimensional periodic medium are described either by the Berry--Zak phase or by the poles and zeros of the surface impedance. We show that both can be read from one geometric object: the line spanned by the field and its flux (the Cauchy data) at an inversion centre. For each band, this line turns as the quasi-momentum runs over the Brillouin zone. Its number of turns, the Maslov index, is fixed by the parities (even or odd) of the Bloch functions at the two band edges, and its parity is the Zak phase. In a gap, the Cauchy line of the solution decaying on one side rotates monotonically with the energy, and an interface state between two crystals is a crossing of two such lines. This gives the known criterion of at most one state per gap in terms of the same lines. Examples with a stratified medium show that the choice of inversion centre changes the interface spectrum. The last section discusses what is missing to extend the construction to higher dimension.

title: Radiation principle for discrete acoustic equation on graphs with several cylindrical outlets to infinity
summary: A discrete analogue of the acoustic equation with a spectral parameter is studied on graphs with several cylindrical outlets to infinity. At infinity in each cylindrical outlet the coefficients of this equation converge exponentially fast to periodic functions. It is assumed that the spectral parameter is fixed and distinct from thresholds and flat bands. We construct a special basis of the continuous spectrum eigenfunctions (bounded solutions of the homogeneous equation that do not belong to l2), introduce the scattering matrix, and establish the radiation principle (a well-posed statement of the problem with radiation conditions at infinity).

title: Absence of Excited Bound States for All Fibers of the Fröhlich Polaron at Weak Coupling
summary: We study the discrete spectrum of the three-dimensional Fröhlich polaron at weak coupling and fixed total momentum. We prove that, for sufficiently small coupling and every total momentum $0<|\xi|\le 1/4$, the ground-state eigenvalue is the only eigenvalue below the essential spectrum. Our proof builds on the analogous zero-momentum result of Seiringer (2023). Combined with that result and the work of Dahlbaek (2017), this implies that, at sufficiently weak coupling, no fiber Hamiltonian has a discrete excited eigenvalue.

title: Finite-strain second-gradient elasticity with an energetic surface: existence of minimizers, incremental theory and elastocapillary beading
summary: We develop a finite-strain theory of second-gradient elasticity for solids with a material surface endowed with its own constitutive energy. The bulk second gradient plays two complementary roles. First, under suitable coercivity assumptions and convexity with respect to the second gradient, we prove the existence of minimizers for nonnegative, lower semicontinuous surface energy densities, without requiring convexity, polyconvexity, positive one-homogeneity, or an upper growth bound on the surface energy. Second, it introduces an intrinsic bulk length scale that affects the onset of instability and wavelength selection. To investigate these effects, we derive an incremental small-on-large formulation in the finitely deformed configuration and apply it to the elastocapillary beading of an axially stretched soft cylinder. For an infinite cylinder and the parameters considered, increasing the second-gradient modulus delays bifurcation and shifts the critical mode towards longer wavelengths. Above a finite threshold of this modulus, the critical stretch saturates in the long-wave limit. The model is implemented in the open-source finite element code OOFEM using C1-continuous isogeometric analysis. Finite-cylinder simulations yield onset stretches in close agreement with the analytical predictions. Selected post-bifurcation branches traced by arc-length continuation exhibit beaded states and supercritical bifurcation at small second-gradient moduli, whereas larger moduli are associated with subcritical bifurcation and the formation of distinct thick and thin segments.

title: A scalable computational framework for PDEs on physical networks
summary: Transport, reaction and wave propagation on physical networks depend on dynamics along edges and interactions at junctions. We present a flexible framework for modeling physical networks at scale. A network calculus expresses edge dynamics and vertex contributions as fields over the whole network. Differential operators satisfy integration by parts-identities that connect local dynamics to global conservation laws, and explicit vertex constraints allow a variety of physical junction conditions. We implement this formalism using the open-source Dedalus spectral framework. This accommodates heterogeneous edge lengths, material properties and spectral resolutions. Initial-value, boundary-value and eigenvalue problems share a parallel solution method that eliminates internal unknowns independently on subgraphs and couples their solutions through shared boundary vertex interfaces. We verify numerical convergence and demonstrate strong and weak scaling on networks with millions of edges. We present applications to localized optical resonances in photonic networks, preferential channel formation during mineral replacement in evolving pore networks, and nonlinear dispersive waves for KdV on a periodic network.

title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
comment: 42 pages, 2 figures. Presents part of the results of arXiv:2609.25477, with an improved treatment of the regularity conditions and of the field equations
summary: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalize the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including a general axial condition that allows for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behavior of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.

title: Induction instead of Feynman diagrams, L-functionals instead of Hilbert space
comment: 11 pages+16 pages of Appendices written by ChatGPT
summary: The main result of this paper is a construction of an inductive process that can replace Feynman diagrams. Combining this result with the notion of the L-functional, one can give an exposition of QED that does not suffer from infrared divergences

title: Remark on residual solutions in the $KBc$ algebra
summary: In this paper we study residual solutions of open bosonic string field theory in the $KBc$ algebra with the auxiliary identities $(\partial^mc)^2=0$ of the ghost field. These solutions are not covered by the classification based on the defining relations alone. We show that the operator which controls the cohomology on the residual family depends only on $s=\gamma_1+\gamma_2$. At positive level $n$, cohomology can appear only on the lines $s=\pm n$. We compute it through level four and find one class at every point of each line $s=-3$ and $s=-4$. These classes give exact polynomial deformations of the residual family. At level six on $s=-6$, the cohomology instead vanishes generically and has dimension two at $(-1,-5)$ and $(-5,-1)$. We also compute the failure of the standard generator redefinition to preserve the auxiliary identities, and discuss the regularization of an explicit residual solution.

title: On Superconformal Index Degenerations and Half-Indices in S-Confining Gauge Theories
summary: We study the $p \rightarrow 0$ limit of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal indices and its relation to half-indices of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories. At the level of special functions, this limit reduces elliptic hypergeometric integrals to basic hypergeometric integrals. The scaling of the flavor fugacities determines the Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions of the chiral multiplets. The gauge multiplet has Neumann boundary conditions. We apply this prescription to s-confining theories with gauge groups $SU(2)$, $USp(2N)$, $G_2$, and $SU(N)$, and recover the half-index identities of several boundary confining dualities, expressed through the Nassrallah-Rahman and Gustafson integrals. For $SU(N)$ with a rank-two antisymmetric chiral, four fundamentals and $N$ antifundamentals, we obtain an analytic proof of the half-index identities proposed by Okazaki and Smith for all $N \geq 5$.

title: 99.9...% of the SU(2) BFSS ground state
summary: We solve for the ground-state wavefunction of the SU(2) BFSS matrix model by applying the Rayleigh-Ritz method to an auxiliary operator $H_{\mathrm{aux}}$. We show that this operator agrees with the Hamiltonian on the ground-state subspace and has a spectral gap. For SU(2) specifically, the representation theory of the singlet sector gives an astronomical reduction in the number of degrees of freedom. This allows us to construct an efficient variational basis whose inner products we compute exactly. We demonstrate the method by computing a state that satisfies rigorous bounds on its energy $E\,g_{\mathrm{YM}}^{-2/3}\leq 4.18\times10^{-8}$ and ground-subspace overlap $\|P_{\ker H}\psi\|^2\geq 0.999997$. We compute ground-state moments with high precision, finding values consistent with the bounds from our matrix bootstrap. Additionally, the state accurately reproduces both the exponent and coefficient of the asymptotic radial probability density predicted by the three-graviton amplitude.

title: Existence of extremal solutions in the 1d conformal bootstrap
summary: Extremal solutions and functionals play an important role in the conformal bootstrap. These are the solutions that saturate unitarity bounds, and the dual functionals that encode the optimal bounds. While they have fundamental theoretical implications, their existence has not been rigorously established. This is particularly subtle in the setting of the full infinite-dimensional bootstrap, i.e. the limit of zero numerical truncation. In this article, we prove that extremal solutions exist for OPE maximisation problems in 1d CFT. These are a large class of generically interacting, unitary, exact solutions of the crossing equation that maximise an OPE coefficient. We also prove that these problems have 'zero duality gap', meaning there exist functionals arbitrarily close to extremality. Our approach is to formulate the bootstrap as a convex optimisation problem in a Hilbert space and apply the Fenchel-Rockafellar theorem.

title: Soft-gluon effective coupling for massive quarks
summary: We present a generalisation of the soft-gluon physical coupling, defined in terms of the strength of soft radiation from a hard dipole, to massive hard emitters. We derive the relation between this coupling and the $\overline{\rm MS}$ coupling through two loops, encompassing all configurations in which both, one, or neither of the hard emitters are massive. We show that the presence of massive emitters introduces additional freedom in the definition of the physical coupling scheme, which we characterise at two-loop order. Our results provide new ingredients for precision QCD resummation in processes involving heavy quarks and for the development of higher-order parton-shower algorithms.

title: Observing Transverse Momentum Broadening from TEECs in Heavy Ion Collisions
summary: We study the azimuthal dependence of transverse energy-energy correlators (TEECs) in dijet events in heavy-ion collisions. In the back-to-back region this observable resolves the energy flow around $\phi=\pi$ and is sensitive to medium-induced momentum broadening and the response of the medium. To isolate final-state effects, we consider a quark-antiquark pair produced in a colour-singlet hard process and propagating through a homogeneous background medium. Starting from the vacuum TMD factorization formula, we combine NLL$'$ resummation with medium modifications at first order in the strong coupling. For the parameters studied, (classical) momentum broadening lowers the back-to-back peak and leaves the distribution elsewhere nearly unchanged, while radiative corrections significantly suppress the peak further and enhance larger angular decorrelations. We additionally include the medium response sourced by each jet, as a mean energy flow. This spreads the deposited energy over the whole azimuth, so that the contribution to the TEEC varies slowly across the back-to-back region, is small at the peak and grows toward larger angles.

title: Entanglement in Collective Neutrino Oscillations on a Quantum Computer
summary: Simulations on a quantum computer have been propounded as a next-generation tool for studying neutrino flavour oscillations in dense environments like supernovae or neutron star mergers. However, quantum advantage hinges on the presence of quantum entanglement in the neutrino ensemble, and it has been argued that such entanglement becomes negligible in the limit of large neutrino number density. Here, we address this question by explicitly simulating the multiparticle dynamics of entangled neutrino ensembles with a varying number of particles, $N$, on both classical and quantum hardware, and comparing our results to those obtained with conventional ``mean-field'' methods based on Boltzmann-type kinetic equations. For simple toy systems, we demonstrate both analytically and numerically that, indeed, the predictions of full multiparticle simulations agree with those of mean-field methods in the large-$N$ limit. Along the way, we develop novel algorithms for the efficient simulation of entangled neutrino gases on both classical and quantum hardware. We then discuss physical situations in which an entangled neutrino system \emph{cannot} be described through mean-field dynamics alone and quantum entanglement therefore becomes phenomenologically relevant. We comment on the conditions under which these scenarios may be realized in supernova cores or neutron star mergers.

title: Opening up derivative baryon-number-violating operators
comment: 33+108 pages; Code and data files available at this https URL
summary: Baryon number violation is our most sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model, typically encoded in higher-dimensional effective operators. Operators involving derivatives are often ignored in phenomenological analyses since they are generically suppressed compared to non-derivative operators. We systematically construct tree-level UV completions of derivative baryon-number-violating operators up to mass dimension 12 in the Standard Model effective field theory (extended by right-handed neutrinos) and show that derivative operators need not be suppressed. Our public code can be used to UV-complete other derivative operators.

title: A Phase-Transition Portal to Enhanced Dark Matter Annihilation
summary: We present a thermal dark matter (DM) scenario in which a phase transition after freeze-out changes both the DM spectrum and the dominant annihilation process, allowing an enhanced present day annihilation rate with suppressed direct detection. We realize this mechanism in a two-Higgs-doublet model extended by a complex scalar singlet, a Majorana fermion, and a heavier Dirac fermion. Before the transition, the Majorana state freezes out through $p$-wave annihilation into singlet scalars. The subsequent transition changes the dark fermion masses and mixing, enabling $s$-wave annihilation through a pseudoscalar portal. The surviving relic differs in mass and composition from the original state. We find relic compatible solutions with present day annihilation rates more than an order of magnitude above the canonical thermal value, without tuning to a mediator resonance, while satisfying direct detection bounds.

title: Exact and hybrid neutrino oscillation probabilities via the evolution operator
summary: We revisit the three-flavor neutrino oscillations in constant-density matter using the evolution matrix expressed in terms of the Lagrange-Sylvester interpolation. Taking advantage of Vieta's formulas for the Hamiltonian of the system, we derive exact closed expressions for the oscillation probabilities $P_{ee}$, $P_{\mu e}$, and $P_{\mu\tau}$, which are concise and simple, and structurally identical to their vacuum counterparts. The CP-violation contribution, proportional to the Jarlskog invariant $\mathcal{J}$, appears as a single, clearly separated term. Our approach does not require introducing neutrino mixing in the medium and avoids using a matter-dependent CP-violation phase, facilitating the separation of genuine CP violation from that induced by matter effects. We explicitly verify that, in the limit $V \to 0$, our expressions for the flavor transition probabilities reduce to the well-known vacuum formulas. The exact structure of the probabilities is preserved if the exact, not very enlightening, trigonometric eigenvalues are replaced by approximate expressions in radicals. We illustrate this hybrid approach with eigenvalues obtained from two successive rotations of the Hamiltonian. For an experiment like DUNE, the hybrid probability values match those of the exact probabilities within absolute errors of about $2\times 10^{-6}$ in all channels and relative errors less than $0.01 \%$ for $P_{ee}$, $P_{\mu e}$, and $P_{\mu\tau}$.

title: Twist-3 and flavor-singlet contributions to $γγ\toπ^{0}η^{(\prime)}$ and $η^{(\prime)}η^{(\prime)}$ in $k_{T}$ factorization
summary: We study two-photon production of the pseudoscalar pairs $\pi^{0}\eta$, $\pi^{0}\eta^{\prime}$, $\eta\eta$, $\eta\eta^{\prime}$, and $\eta^{\prime}\eta^{\prime}$ at center-of-mass energies $2<Q<4\,\mathrm{GeV}$ in $k_{T}$ factorization, including the chirally enhanced twist-3 amplitudes and the two-gluon component of the $\eta^{(\prime)}$. The twist-3 amplitudes raise the hard cross sections by about an order of magnitude in all five channels. They bring $\eta\eta$ close to the Belle data, while $\pi^{0}\eta$ stays 3 to 5 times below and falls too slowly with energy. Varying the two-gluon distribution amplitude within its uncertainty changes the cross sections by about 2% in $\pi^{0}\eta$ and $\eta\eta$ but by up to 24% in the $\eta^{\prime}$ channels, making them its probe. The hard and handbag mechanisms each give nearly constant ratios $\sigma(\pi^{0}\eta)/\sigma(\pi^{0}\pi^{0})$ and $\sigma(\eta\eta)/\sigma(\pi^{0}\pi^{0})$, whereas below $3.2\,\mathrm{GeV}$ the measured $\pi^{0}\eta$ ratio lies above both predictions and the $\eta\eta$ ratio below them. Adding the handbag amplitude coherently, with its modulus fixed by the pion and kaon channels and its phase fitted, reproduces the $\pi^{0}\eta$ ratio up to $4\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and the $\eta\eta$ ratio below $2.8\,\mathrm{GeV}$, and steepens $\sigma(\pi^{0}\eta)$ to a $Q^{-n}$ dependence with $n=9.7\pm1.6$, against the measured $10.5\pm1.2\pm0.5$. The energy dependence of the cross section ratios can thus be understood as the interference of two mechanisms of comparable size.

title: Spiral momentum spectra and spin asymmetry in vacuum pair production driven by phase-modulated elliptically polarized electric fields
summary: We study vacuum electron--positron pair production in phase-modulated elliptically polarized electric fields using the quantum kinetic equations. We analyze how the modulation amplitude, frequency, ellipticity, and modulation form affect the spin-resolved momentum spectra and the spin asymmetry. Cosine-type modulation can deform ring-shaped momentum distributions into spiral patterns. This deformation depends nonmonotonically on the modulation amplitude and frequency and is most pronounced for circular polarization. In the transverse momentum plane, the spin-resolved yields favor the spin channel along the direction of field handedness. Reversing the field handedness would reverse the favored channel while leaving the total yield unchanged. Sine-type modulation preserves ring-shaped and mirror-symmetric spectra approximately, however, it leads to a stronger dependence of the spin asymmetry on the modulation amplitude than cosine-type modulation does. These results show that phase modulation and ellipticity can control the momentum spectra patterns in vacuum pair production. Moreover, phase modulation can also affect the degree of spin asymmetry.

title: Probing flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions with the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos
Production of hidden-charm molecular candidates with hidden strangeness in $B_s^0$ decays
summary: We study the production of spin-one $D_{s0}^*(2317)\bar D_s^*$, $D_{s1}(2460)\bar D_s^*$, and $D_{s1}(2536)\bar D_s^*$ molecular candidates in $B_s^0$ decays with an accompanying $\eta$, providing a complementary probe of their structure and production mechanisms. The meson-loop rescattering amplitudes are constructed from factorized weak sources and heavy-hadron chiral interactions. Constituent couplings are estimated using threshold-dependent compositeness relations, and the associated input uncertainties are propagated to the predicted rates. Opposite-$C$-parity partner hypotheses are included with inherited benchmark parameters. We calculate the branching fractions for two relative signs. Over the cutoff range $2\leq\alpha\leq5$, the larger central branching fractions reach several $10^{-6}$ to several $10^{-5}$, suggesting potential accessibility in future experimental measurements.

title: Renormalon-chain contributions to two-point correlators of nonlocal quark currents and light-meson distribution amplitudes
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, 10 references. Contribution to the proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP 2026), July 30 -- August 5, 2026, Natal, Brazil
summary: In the framework of QCD sum rules, we study the endpoint slopes of the leading-twist distribution amplitudes in the large-$\beta_0$ approximation for the pion and the longitudinally polarized $\rho$ meson. To this end, we compute the two-point massless correlator of non-local composite vector quark currents with the gluon lines dressed by chains of one-loop fermion bubbles. This correlator depends on the Bjorken fraction $x$ associated with the composite current and, within the large-$\beta_0$ approximation, provides the dominant contribution in each order of perturbation theory. We derive an inequality for the second Gegenbauer moments of these distribution amplitudes that agrees with predictions from lattice QCD.

title: Stimulated Axion Decay around Primordial Black Holes and the Diffuse Radio Background
summary: We study stimulated axion decay in dense axion halos around primordial black holes (PBHs), assuming that both PBHs and axions contribute to dark matter. We construct the axion density profile by matching a hydrogenic soliton-like core dominated by the PBH potential to the $r^{-9/4}$ spike produced by secondary infall. We also impose an inner cutoff at the innermost stable circular orbit. We derive local Boltzmann equations for the number densities of photons and axions, including spontaneous and stimulated decay, inverse decay, photon escape, and axion filling. We solve these equations numerically and with a semi-analytic approximation. Stimulated emission occurs within an inner region where photon amplification overcomes escape. We calculate the photon emission from an individual PBH halo and integrate it over the population of PBHs throughout cosmic history. By requiring the resulting diffuse radio spectrum not to exceed the radio background measured by ARCADE~2, we derive upper bounds on the fraction of dark matter in PBHs. The bounds are strongest at intermediate PBH masses and apply over a wider mass range as the coupling between axions and photons increases.

title: Restoration of rotational symmetry in light-front dynamics
summary: Solving the bound state problem in the framework of the light-front dynamics (with the state vector defined in the light-front plane t+z=0), one finds that after truncation - representing approximately the state vector by a finite number of the Fock components, the binding energies become to depend on projection of the angular momentum on the z-axes. This is so called violation of rotational symmetry in light-front dynamics. It is shown that the physical solution is the superposition of these states with some well defined coefficients. For a test, we also solve the Bethe-Salpeter equation and projecting its solution on the light-front, we find the wave functions which do not suffer from violation of the rotation invariance. Comparison with them of solution in the form of superposition shows that not only binding energies but also the wave functions themselves are described by the superpositions of the split states fairly well.

title: Roles of $f_0(980)$ and $a_0(980)$ in the process $Λ_c^+ \to pK_S^0K_S^0$: a clean probe of the $K\bar K$ final-state interaction
summary: Based on the Belle measurement of $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK_S^0K_S^0$, we study the contributions of the light scalar mesons $f_0(980)$ and $a_0(980)$, dynamically generated from the $S$-wave pseudoscalar meson--pseudoscalar meson interaction within the chiral unitary approach, to the threshold enhancement in the $K_S^0K_S^0$ invariant mass squared distribution, and examine the possible contribution of the intermediate $\Sigma(1620)$ resonance in the $pK_S^0$ subsystem. We first argue that the $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK_S^0K_S^0$ channel is a cleaner probe of the $K\bar K$ final-state interaction than the charged channel $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK^+K^-$, since the $\phi$ and $\Lambda^*$ contributions are forbidden and the $\Sigma(1620)$ and $\Sigma(1660)$ couple weakly to the $\bar{K}N$ channel. The threshold enhancement in the $K_S^0K_S^0$ invariant mass squared distribution is well described by the $S$-wave $K^0\bar K^0$ final-state interaction alone, with the $f_0(980)$ contribution dominating while that of $a_0(980)$ is small, supporting the interpretation of $f_0(980)$ as a $K\bar K$ hadronic molecular state. Future high-precision measurements by Belle~II and the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility will help test the roles of the $f_0(980)$ and $a_0(980)$ and of the possible $\Sigma(1620)$ contribution in this process.

title: Collins-Soper kernel at large $b$ from Chiral Perturbation Theory
summary: We construct effective operators for transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distributions in Chiral Perturbation Theory. The operators constructed from pion and nucleon fields possess the main properties of the QCD operators, including multiplicatively renormalizable rapidity divergences. Extracting the leading rapidity divergence, we find the expression for the Collins-Soper kernel at large $b$ and at the low-energy normalization point, which is model-independent up to an additive constant. In this regime, the Collins-Soper kernel has a nearly constant behavior. We also find that at large $b$ it depends on the isospin channel and on the hadron type, although this dependence is numerically very small.

title: Spin Correlations in $t\bar{t}$ Production and Decay at the LHC in Perturbative QCD
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. With minor differences, it matches the submitted proceedings for talks given at The 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026), 4 - 8 May 2026, Bologna, Italy, and The XII edition of QCD@Work, International Workshop on QCD, theory and experiment (QCD@Work 2026), 16 - 19 June 2026, Trani, Italy
summary: Among recent developments in top-quark physics at the LHC, the production of top-quark pairs near threshold has attracted considerable attention, partly due to tensions between data and theoretical predictions. We show that reliable predictions for threshold-sensitive observables, such as spin correlations and the differential distribution in the $t\bar{t}$ invariant mass, can be obtained in perturbation theory by retaining the first few powers of $\alpha_s/v$, where $v$ is the relative velocity of the top quarks. Applying this approach to reweight nominal Monte Carlo predictions for spin-sensitive observables, we find good agreement with data. We also discuss how threshold effects, including bound-state contributions, can be incorporated on an event-by-event basis into fully differential Monte Carlo event generators.

title: Nucleon-resonance contributions to the $p\bar{p}\toη_cη$ reaction
summary: Within an effective Lagrangian approach, we investigate the associated charmonium production reaction $p\bar{p}\to\eta_c\eta$ from threshold up to $\sqrt{s}=5.00\,\mathrm{GeV}$, incorporating intermediate contributions from the ground-state nucleon and the nucleon resonances $N(1535)$, $N(1650)$, $N(1895)$, and $N(1710)$. The effective resonance parameters are constrained by the BESIII measurement of the crossed decay $\eta_c\to p\bar{p}\eta$ for both the constructive (Solution C) and destructive (Solution D) radiative-interference solutions. Using these decay-constrained parameters, we predict the total and differential Born cross sections for the $p\bar{p}\to\eta_c\eta$ reaction. We show that coherent resonance exchanges dominate the near-threshold production dynamics and significantly enhance the total cross section compared to the pure nucleon-exchange contribution, which suffers from a strong dynamical cancellation. As the collision energy increases, the rapidly growing nucleon contribution progressively dilutes the resonance terms, reducing the relative difference between the total cross sections for Solutions C and D. Furthermore, while the pure nucleon-exchange amplitude exhibits an exact dynamical zero at $\theta=90^\circ$ due to the pseudoscalar coupling structure, resonance exchanges fill this node in the predicted angular distributions, providing an observable test of the underlying exchange mechanisms. These predictions can be tested in future antiproton annihilation experiments at $\bar{\mathrm{P}}\mathrm{ANDA}$.

title: Parton density functions for future electron-positron colliders
comment: 6 pages, contribution to proceedings of ICHEP-2026
summary: Precision QED radiative corrections are critical for the physics programs of future high-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders. We review the state-of-the-art QED parton density function (PDF) formalism for resumming collinear photon and pair emissions. Our numerical analysis of initial-state radiation (ISR) highlights the slow convergence of the perturbative series and the growing significance of pair production at higher orders. Finally, we emphasize the need to implement these theoretical refinements into modern Monte Carlo generators to meet the stringent precision demands of upcoming experimental measurements.

title: An interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles
summary: We conjecture a novel interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles: $\theta^{}_{23} = \left(\theta^{}_{12} + \theta^{}_{13}\right)/2 + \pi/8$, which predicts $\theta^{}_{23} = 43.46^{+0.51^\circ}_{-0.52^\circ}$ with inputs of the latest JUNO and Daya Bay precision data. A simple ansatz is proposed to derive this phenomenologically favored and experimentally testable angle relation, and present a new expansion of the lepton flavor mixing matrix in powers of a single small parameter as a by-product.

title: Thermal Field Theory for General Equilibrium Density Matrices
comment: Invited chapter of the Quantum Field Theory section of "Comprehensive Quantum Physics" (Elsevier); 28 pages
summary: Thermal field theory (TFT) is the combination of statistical mechanics and relativistic quantum field theory. This (book) chapter provides a pedagogical introduction to (and a review of) TFT for general equilibrium density matrices, which allow arbitrary values not only of temperature and chemical potentials, but also of average angular momentum. A general technique to compute ensemble averages is illustrated. Path-integral methods are developed to study the partition function and the thermal Green's functions of general operators, with an arbitrary number of points, in all field theories of physical relevance.

title: Interference effects in MSSM Higgs boson searches at low $tanβ$: the $gg\to H\to WW, ZZ, hh$ and $gg \to A \to Zh$ channels
summary: The LHC limits on the heavy neutral Higgs bosons of the minimal supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model, which are particularly relevant at low values of the ratio of vacuum expectation values $\tan\beta$, have been obtained in the narrow-width approximation, without including the interference between the pure Higgs signal and the QCD background. We study the interference of the resonant heavy neutral CP-even $H$ and CP-odd $A$ boson contributions with the non-resonant gluon-fusion amplitudes in the processes $gg\to VV$ with $V=W,Z$, $gg \to hh$ and $gg\to Zh$ at low $\tan\beta$, $1\le \tan\beta \le 6$. We work at leading order but with the exact top-quark mass dependence, and with the longitudinal $VV$ and $Zh$ amplitudes obtained from the Goldstone-boson equivalence theorem that lead to loop form factors similar to those appearing in $gg\to hh$. The lineshapes in the four search channels are governed by a simple complex parameter $\kappa$, the ratio of the resonant to non-resonant amplitudes at the peak. Because the $H$ and $A$ bosons couple weakly to the considered final states, while being broadened by their decays to top quarks, $|\kappa|$ drops to values of a few for masses of $0.5$--$1$ TeV, even though the total widths remain at the percent level. The interference then increases the signal rates by up to tens of per cent, and distorts their lineshapes. For the present ATLAS (and presumably CMS) Run II exclusion limits, the net effect is nevertheless rather modest, except at the high-mass end of the $H\to hh$ contour, but it becomes important for the masses that will be probed at the high-luminosity LHC.

title: Uncovering TeV-scale dark matter with Z-fusion at a muon collider
summary: We demonstrate the advantage of the $Z$-boson fusion channel at a high-energy, high-luminosity muon collider in eliciting signals of a TeV-scale scalar dark matter (DM) particle. The utility of such a set-up lies in (a)the attainability of high centre-of-mass energy ($\approx 10 ~\rm TeV$), (b)the likely availability of large integrated luminosity ($\gtrsim 10~ab^{-1}$), and (c)the facility for efficient detection of very forward tagged muons. Our analysis is based on the process $\mu^+ \mu^- \rightarrow \mu^+ \mu^-$ + missing energy, driven by $Z$-fusion. We present the results in the context of (i) a scenario characterised by dimension-6 effective couplings, and (ii) an inert doublet model. After filtering each scenario through its associated constraints, we find that it is possible to achieve a signal significance of about 6.7$\sigma$ in case (i) and about 5.5$\sigma$ in case (ii), for DM particle masses $\approx$ 1 TeV and an integrated luminosity of $10 ~ ab^{-1}$.

title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
comment: 14 pages, 1 figure. Webinar presentation: this https URL
summary: A minimal realisation of warm inflation, even within the Standard Model, assumes that the inflaton $\phi$ couples via the effective operator $\phi\, G\tilde G$. We show that the SM solutions are in tension with the plasma calculation (as each sphaleron transition releases an energy much larger than the temperature) and with the assumed effective operator description. Embedding $\phi$ as the Goldstone boson of a renormalizable Peccei-Quinn theory requires an anomaly coefficient $\gtrsim100$, implying a Landau pole for QCD. These tensions are relaxed for more strongly coupled dark gauge sectors.

title: Chiral Response of QCD Topology across the Thermal Crossover
summary: We introduce a novel relation connecting the light-quark-mass derivative of the topological susceptibility in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) to the connected correlation between the squared topological charge and the integrated light-quark scalar density. This relation gives direct access to the chiral response of QCD topology---the local logarithmic light-quark-mass derivative of the susceptibility---from a single ensemble at fixed quark masses for each temperature, without additional simulations at shifted masses. Applying this relation to $(2+1)$-flavor lattice QCD at $m_\pi\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$ over temperatures ranging from well below to well above the chiral crossover, we find that the response rises rapidly through the crossover from approximately unity toward two. This evolution corresponds to a change from nearly linear to nearly quadratic dependence of the topological susceptibility on the light-quark mass. Using the chiral response as the exponent of a local power law in the light-quark mass, we determine its effective amplitude from the topological susceptibility. This amplitude exhibits a maximum near the crossover temperature, reflecting the competition between the decreasing topological susceptibility and the increasing chiral response. These results reveal a thermal reorganization of the quark-mass dependence of QCD topology beyond the suppression of topological fluctuations alone.

title: Dynamical gluon mass generation, the Schwinger mechanism, spontaneous symmetry breaking, and color confinement in the linear covariant gauges of QCD
summary: We critically re-examine the Kugo-Ojima (KO) scenario for color confinement and identify several inconsistencies and a crucial error in its derivation. Within the KO framework, under customary assumptions, we show that the BRST quartet structure incorporates a unique mechanism for dynamical gluon mass generation -- namely, the Schwinger mechanism, in the formulation developed by Aguilar, Binosi, Ferreira, and Papavassiliou (ABFP). We show that the Schwinger mechanism is a Higgs mechanism, in that it occurs together with the spontaneous breaking of the global gauge charge, as it should. The ABFP bound state is the associated (unphysical) composite Goldstone boson. The zero-momentum value of the gluon propagator evaluated in the Pinch Technique--Background-Field Method (PT-BFM) naturally emerges in the derivation, setting a Renormalization-Group invariant scale for mass generation and suggesting a new nonperturbative interpretation of the PT-BFM. BRST symmetry takes over the role of the broken symmetry, while the color symmetry of the spectrum remains unbroken. We obtain a unique, well-defined, unbroken, BRST-exact asymptotic color charge operator that realizes the confinement of color in the sense of the absence of colored asymptotic states from the BRST cohomology. Still within the KO framework, we take the first fundamental step towards a proof of the nonperturbative unitarity of the linear covariant gauges of QCD, and we discuss the experimental evidence in favor of the Schwinger mechanism. We lay down the foundations for a unified theory of gauge-boson mass generation in the linear covariant gauges of Yang-Mills theories.

title: Kinematic Reconstruction of Top-Quark Pairs Using Analytical and Machine-Learning Methods with CMS Open Data
summary: The reconstruction of the top-quark-pair ($t\bar{t}$) kinematics in the dilepton $t\bar{t}$ decay channel is challenging due to the presence of two undetected neutrinos. In this work, existing kinematic reconstruction methods used by the CMS Collaboration are studied using a Monte Carlo sample with $t\bar{t}$ events from CMS Open Data at a centre-of-mass energy of 7 TeV. An improved version of the loose kinematic reconstruction, LKRv2, is developed by imposing more stringent requirements on the jet-lepton pairing entering the reconstruction. A further modification, LKRv3, exploits the kinematic similarity between the dilepton and neutrino-pair systems and improves the resolution of the reconstructed $t\bar{t}$ invariant mass relative to the baseline LKR by $7\%$, with smaller improvements for the transverse momentum and rapidity of $t\bar{t}$. In addition, two machine-learning (ML) based approaches are developed using a residual multilayer perceptron and a conditional normalizing flow. Relative to LKRv3, they improve the resolution of the invariant mass, transverse momentum and rapidity by approximately $30\%$, $20\%$ and $15\%$, respectively. In particular, a resolution of 30 GeV is achieved for the reconstructed invariant mass of $t\bar{t}$ near the production threshold. A dedicated generator-level study and a generator-to-detector transfer test demonstrate that the ML approaches learn a genuine physics-driven correction to the $\nu\bar{\nu}$ approximation, rather than merely exploiting detector-specific effects. These results demonstrate the strong potential of ML-based approaches for improving the reconstruction of dilepton $t\bar{t}$ events, while identifying the neutrino-pair approximation as an important limitation on the achievable resolution.

title: Emergence and polymer physics of the center-vortex network: Confronting SU(4) lattice Yang-Mills theory
summary: The geometric organization and statistical properties of center-vortex networks provide a window into the infrared dynamics underlying confinement in Yang-Mills theory. Motivated by this connection, we investigate new consequences of a previously proposed confinement mechanism based on physically equivalent elementary Cartan fluxes. We show that, in the percolating phase, these fluxes dynamically reorganize into center-charge sectors whose dominant vortex tensions satisfy a Casimir scaling law, similar to that observed for confining string tensions. We then confront this result with the first nontrivial Yang-Mills case: the doubly charged vortex chains recently observed in SU(4) lattice simulations. To extract the parameters needed to connect the lattice ensemble with the effective description, we characterize how center-vortex chains grow and bend in SU(3) and SU(4) using polymer-inspired techniques not previously applied to center vortices. We find good quantitative agreement for the SU(4) doubly charged sector, providing further evidence for the proposed mechanism.
